comparison: Perfect claim overlap (C64-C69, C95) on histogram-matching analyses. OpenEval finds the analysis SUPPORTED with appropriate methodology, while peer reviewers also mark SUPPORTED but note overall methodological uncertainties about event detection may indirectly affect confidence.

Perfect claim overlap (C121-C126) on alpha-beta dissociations and spectral characteristics. OpenEval finds these contextual claims SUPPORTED with appropriate citations, while peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN and specifically request (Essential Revision #5) comparative analysis with alpha and gamma to establish frequency specificity.

Perfect claim overlap (C127-C131) on speculative implications for stimulation studies. OpenEval marks UNCERTAIN noting these are predictions rather than demonstrated results, and peer reviewers also mark UNCERTAIN, noting validity depends on resolution of core methodological concerns.

Perfect claim overlap (C133-C145) on methodological details for human detection task. OpenEval finds methods SUPPORTED and adequately described, while peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN, indicating (Essential Revision #1) that provided methods are insufficient and requesting additional information about MEG source locations and somatosensory responses.

High overlap (C3, C34-C35, C91) on discrete beta events vs. averaged spectrograms. OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED by visual evidence in Figure 2, while peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN with significant concern (Essential Revision #2) about whether analysis truly distinguishes bursts from dynamic amplitude modulation, requesting additional evidence including bimodal histograms and phase-preservation analysis.

High overlap (C5, C19, C55-C58, C62, C94) on timing of most recent event. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by Figure 8 analyses showing ~200ms window, while peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN, noting that broader methodological concerns (Essential Revisions #2, #3, #4) about event detection and lack of comparison with conventional power analyses indirectly affect confidence.

Substantial overlap (C36-C43) on event feature distributions and 6X median cutoff. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by systematic analyses in Figures 4-5, while peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN, raising concerns (Essential Revision #3) about threshold-based approach potentially misclassifying sustained oscillations and requesting comparison with alternative definitions requiring minimum intervals or amplitude relaxation.

Substantial overlap (C6-C7, C21-C22) on cross-species consistency. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED noting core relationships consistent across datasets, while peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN, questioning (Essential Revision #1) whether recordings are from task-relevant populations and whether functional relevance is established.

Substantial overlap (C23, C25, C27, C29-C33, C88) on basic power-behavior correlations. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with robust statistical evidence across datasets, while peer reviewers mark SUPPORTED but request (Essential Revision #4) comparison with regular power analyses to determine if event features provide additional predictive value.

Substantial overlap (C47-C53) on event rate statistical comparisons. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by comprehensive analyses in Figures 6-7, while peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN, questioning (Essential Revision #6) the proportion of zero-event trials and whether correlations would differ when including these trials.

Substantial overlap (C76-C82) on congruency between event definitions. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by ~80% overlap validation in Figure 11, while peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN, noting (Essential Revision #3) that short IEIs suggest doublets/triplets and questioning consistency with behavioral outcome differences.

Moderate overlap (C4, C45-C46, C54, C92-C93) on event rate superiority. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with strong statistical evidence and effect sizes, while peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN, raising critical questions (Essential Revisions #4, #6) about comparison with conventional power and handling of zero-event trials.

Moderate overlap (C70-C71, C73, C85, C118) on bursty/non-rhythmic mechanism. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by multiple complementary analyses including Hilbert transform and Fano Factor, while peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN, questioning interpretation of short IEIs and requesting clarification about doublets/triplets.

Partial overlap (C96, C103-C104) on attention and timing synthesis. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with C104 noted as more speculative, while peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN, indicating mechanistic interpretations depend on validity of event detection and specificity of neural populations (Essential Revisions #1, #2).

Partial overlap (C86-C87) on Hilbert transform rhythmicity analysis. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as particularly strong evidence for bursty mechanism, while peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN, noting this addresses their concerns (Essential Revision #2) but requesting additional specific analyses including amplitude envelope histograms and phase-preservation.

Partial overlap (C83-C84) on robustness across definitions. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as important validation, while peer reviewers mark SUPPORTED, acknowledging this demonstrates findings are not entirely dependent on specific detection method.

Partial overlap (C107-C108, C110) on mechanistic inferences. OpenEval marks UNCERTAIN noting behavioral correlations are established but mechanistic interpretation is inferential, while peer reviewers also mark UNCERTAIN, indicating concerns about source localization (Essential Revision #1) affect which mechanistic interpretations are plausible.

Minimal overlap (C24, C26, C28) on power-behavior correlations, but peer review also includes methodological claims (C134-C135). OpenEval finds statistical evidence SUPPORTED, while peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN with critical concern (Essential Revision #1) about unclear origin of beta events and insufficient source localization information.

Minimal overlap (C116-C117) on cutoff variation analyses. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED showing systematic crossover at ~3X median, while peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN as part of broader concerns (Essential Revision #3) about threshold-based approach and request for alternative definitions.

Minimal overlap (C114-C115) on bimodality and stereotypy. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED noting careful reasoning despite lack of bimodality, while peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN, with concerns about threshold approach potentially misclassifying sustained oscillations as part of Essential Revision #3.

Minimal overlap (C105-C106) on phase-alignment mechanism. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as appropriate inference from bursty/non-rhythmic evidence, while peer reviewers mark UNCERTAIN as part of broader mechanistic interpretation concerns dependent on event detection validity.

Minimal overlap (C98) on novelty claims. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with appropriate qualifier 'to our knowledge', while peer reviewers mark SUPPORTED for background claims without specific challenge to novelty assertion.

Minimal overlap (C33) on control analysis ruling out motor/criterion confounds. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by Figure 1 supplement showing no CR vs FA difference, while peer reviewers mark SUPPORTED for basic power-behavior relationships without specifically addressing this control.

OpenEval finds C132 (summary inference about event features vs. mean power) SUPPORTED as appropriate synthesis of comprehensive analyses. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, though related concerns appear in Essential Revisions #4 and #6.

Peer reviewers mark C111-C113 (alternative mechanistic speculations) as UNCERTAIN, noting source localization concerns affect plausibility. OpenEval addresses these claims within R13 as appropriately speculative but does not have a separate result for this specific subset.
